summary: Seven-acre Port of San Francisco waterfront park on the former shipyard shoreline between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street, built around historic Slipway 4 and two gantry cranes with a pocket beach, lawn and Bay Trail link. Planned from 2011, built under a $17.8 million contract awarded to Gordon N. Ball in November 2018, and opened September 30, 2020 at a total cost of $36.7 million; the playgrounds and dog run followed on December 12, 2025.

milestones.text: Park first envisioned in the Port's Waterfront Land Use Plan; later carried in the 2010 Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan and 2012 Blue Greenway Planning and Design Guidelines

Port Commission awards the master planning and preliminary design contract (AECOM, selected competitively); initial estimate about $30 million for the whole park, with $10 million secured from the 2008 Parks GO Bond
Park design approved by the City's Waterfront Design Advisory Committee and the BCDC Design Review Board

Port Commission approves the Crane Cove Park project and the fourth and final sale of 2008 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds ($8,695,000); estimated total project cost $31,475,904; Phase I to deliver about five acres of an eventual ten-acre park
Port Commission awards the site preparation contract (Contract 2740); site preparation starts November 2016 and is complete by 2017
Bids opened for the park improvements contract (No. 2781) all significantly exceed the engineer's estimate and are rejected
Port Commission informational report: $9.3 million spent to date, $36.6 million total budget across five bid packages, Phase I only
Resolution 18-61 awards Contract 2812 (Park Improvements and 19th St Parking Lot) to Gordon N. Ball, Inc. for $17,845,000 plus a 10% contingency; park scheduled to open at the beginning of 2020
Hazardous materials abatement completed (Port project page timeline)
Crane Cove Park opens to the public
Opening reported: seven acres, pocket beach, lawn, engineered for up to 28 inches of sea level rise
19th and Georgia Street construction, the Building 49 core-and-shell retrofit and the permanent public restrooms completed

Port opens the Rigger's Yard and Tot Lot play areas and the off-leash dog run, after the San Francisco Parks Alliance's fundraising fell short and the Port redirected Southern Waterfront Beautification Fund money

costs.what: Total cost of the entire Crane Cove Park project, funded by $25.9 million from the 2008 and 2012 Parks Bonds and $10.8 million in grants and Port sources
Contract 2812 (park improvements and 19th St parking lot) awarded to Gordon N. Ball, Inc.; total authorization $19,629,500 with 10% contingency
Total project funding stated at contract award, with completion anticipated at the beginning of 2020
Fourth and final sale of 2008 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds for Crane Cove Park
Estimated Phase I project cost at the October 2015 approval
Budget set aside from park funding for the Building 49 scope (restrooms, aquatic center, concessions), with a further ~$4 million hoped for from Parks Alliance fundraising
Baker Street Foundation donation for the playgrounds and dog run, most of which the San Francisco Parks Alliance mismanaged before closing in 2025 (CBS report; the Port then shifted internal funds)

facts.value: approximately 7 (Phase I; the 2015 approval described an eventual 10-acre park, the 2018 report an approximately eight-acre site)
Between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street; entrance at 18th/19th and Illinois
AECOM (master planning, preliminary and final design, construction support)
Gordon N. Ball, Inc. (park improvements, Contract 2812)

Pocket beach with Bay access for kayaks and paddle boards, restored Slipway 4, two historic gantry cranes, multi-purpose lawn with picnic and barbecue areas, Crane Plaza, dog run, two play areas, restrooms, Bay Trail / Blue Greenway link, sediment cap along the shoreline
Designed for 50 years of projected sea level rise to at least 2065 (+28 inches)
2008 and 2012 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds, Port capital and grants; the 2008 bond allocated $33.5 million to Port waterfront parks

Historic Building 49 retrofitted for restrooms, an aquatic (human-powered boating) center and concessions; core-and-shell work done July 2021; the Port's park page lists a YMCA Dogpatch wellness center and Dogpatch Paddle rentals adjacent to the park

Delivered by the Port under the 2010 Preferred Master Plan, separate from Brookfield's 28-Acre Site; the plan's two development 'pads' along Illinois Street were dropped at community request during park design review

open_questions: No image is hosted: the Port's park photographs carry no stated license, and no Wikimedia Commons or public-domain photo was checked in this pass. The Port's opening-day photos are linked from the sources.

The 2015 approval spoke of a ten-acre park delivered in phases; whether a Phase II (the remaining acreage, to be funded from IFD proceeds per the 2018 report) is still planned is not stated in any later document found.
The exact total spent through 2025, including the playground and dog-run work, is not published; the $36.7 million figure is from the FY2024-33 capital plan.
